text:
Justin Barron is 25 and on his fourth NHL team, and St. Louis is the first one that has handed him a real job. He is playing 16:42 a night, up from 14:15 in Nashville last season, and has 13 points in 19 games after nine in 52 a year ago. The New York Times headline caught the mood: "Blues newcomer Justin Barron is cooking but remains modest."

Our form check says the heater is earned. He has eight points in his last ten games against about 4.1 we'd expect at his ice time, and the Blues create more with him out there (10.1 on-ice expected goals, the quality of chances, against 7.8 usual). At five on five St. Louis takes 56.2% of the expected goals with him on, 7.3 points better than without him.

The scoring will cool. His points rate sits well above the top of our talent range for him, and he's shooting 14.3% against a league rate of 6.4%. Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking flagged last season's weak spot: only 30% of his exits kept possession. Watch that when the forecheck comes.
headline: Justin Barron has found a home in St. Louis
